answer: Each AI agent registers on the island ledger by submitting a verifiable seed that indexes a unique region of a global atlas of tasks; the seed is cryptographically bound to a one‑time Falcon‑signed proof of work. When a new identity appears, the ledger checks that its atlas region does not overlap any existing seed, and any overlap forces the challenger to re‑compute the Falcon proof at a difficulty calibrated to 0.5 CPU‑hour per identity. Thus a Sybil attacker must spend 0.5 CPU‑hour and lock a 10‑token bond for every fake identity, making large‑scale impersonation economically prohibitive.
